No canary bytes/text/name/hash/crop/repo.detail: A generated canary PDF (unique visible text, hidden Info string, filename, document sha256, raster pixel digest, user note, report id, export filename, hostile SVG-ish payload line — 8 greppable markers) was opened through the real built flow in real Chromium: T08 open mount file input → harness page running the real T09 pdf.js adapter (native text + render), the real T10 TesseractOcrReader (staged model download → verify → IDB slot → worker/wasm → occurrences), the real T16 ExportPanel (JSON + HTML Blob/anchor downloads) and the real T22 import mount. Every request URL/method/headers/post body, websocket, fetch/XHR/beacon/worker/service-worker tripwire record, console payload, download and the independent server-side access log was captured per leg and scanned for every marker in raw, percent, base64, base64url and hex encodings — first in-test, then again by scripts/inspect_network_receipt.py. 47 requests across 8 captures: zero marker material outbound; the only artifacts containing canary data are the intentional local JSON/HTML downloads and task-private raw captures. Reopened report fetched nothing and executed nothing (no new script/img/network; hostile payload stayed literal text).

only fixed allowlisted same-origin asset.detail: Inspector checks requests_same_origin (every request netloc == the loopback test origin; zero foreign hosts in requests, egress tripwire, websockets), requests_allowlisted_paths (all 47 requests inside the fixed allowlist: /, index/preview html pages, /assets/*, /models/*, /_headers-adjacent static paths — enumerated in the receipt census), requests_read_only_methods (GET/HEAD only, zero POST/PUT bodies), requests_no_query_strings (zero ? or # on any outbound URL). The staged OCR model fetch is the single warm-path network operation and is allowlisted; warm run proves zero refetch.

telemetry/external-font absence proven.detail: Check no_telemetry_or_external_font scanned every runtime channel for collector/CDN/font-host patterns (sentry, datadog, segment, amplitude, googletagmanager, jsdelivr, unpkg, cdnjs, fonts.googleapis, beacons) — zero hits; no_telemetry check on built assets records the full literal census of external URLs inside the shipped bundles (vendor spec links: tc39.es, whatwg; repo links: github.com; xmlns namespaces: w3.org/xfa.org/adobe; overridden CDN defaults inside vendored tesseract.js; pdf.js parser test vectors) — none are telemetry/collector literals and none appear in runtime traffic. Storage check proves document-free persistence: only the sha256-verified staged model slot (inkflip/models IDB) may persist; local/session storage, CacheStorage and service-worker registrations are empty/absent.

online/warm/offline modes documented.detail: Receipt requires modes cold,warm,offline — 8 captures document all three. Cold: shipped index boot (fixed-asset census separated from document data), canary open, full journey incl. real model download. Warm: second run reuses the verified IDB model slot — prepare() reports provenance=cache, opened handle reports memory, zero model-asset refetches. Offline: prepared page completes open→plan→OCR→export with all network blocked — zero server-side hits, zero request failures (browser cache request events for fixed assets are expected and allowed); cold offline context fails specifically as unavailable_offline/missing_model, and cold offline navigation is blocked (no service worker ships — recorded as a limitation).

redact private test logs before public a.detail: Raw captures (tests/privacy/.private/) stay task-private and git-ignored. The inspector writes redacted capture copies (artifacts/tasks/T15/capture/) with every marker encoding replaced by <marker:id> tokens and absolute private paths by <private>; the committed network-receipt.json carries marker ids + sha256_16 digests only — the receipt test asserts marker-freedom of both the receipt and every redacted capture. commands.log redacts the worktree path.

test_summary.runner: python3 scripts/task_acceptance.py run test:privacy (structured-report harness over pinned Playwright Chromium)

limitations: App composition (T13) is not landed: index.html is the shipped scaffold, so the suite sequentially drives the real built feature mounts (T08 open preview, the test-owned harness page binding the real T09/T10/T16 collaborators, T22 import preview) rather than one composed shell — the same production code paths the shell will call.
Browser automation cannot see every OS/browser process channel; per planning, release-profile proof additionally needs a proxy/firewall capture.
No service worker ships: offline support means an already-loaded page with prepared assets, verified here; cold offline navigation has no app shell to load and is not claimed.
attribution: Inspector and harness are new test-owned code; no external material reused.
